record.original_question: Let d_n = (p_{n+1} - p_n)/2, where p_n is the nth prime. Determine whether the sequence (d_n) contains infinitely many primes, whether it contains values of the form n!, and whether it contains values of the form n^n. More generally, for higher-order derived sequences formed from prime gaps, ask the same questions.

evidence.quote: Let dn be the distance between two consecutive primes ... Does dn contain an infinite number of primes? Does dn contain numbers of the form n! ? But of the form nn ? ... The same questions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p_n$ denote the $n$th prime number ($p_1=2, p_2=3, p_3=5,\dots$), and define the sequence of half-gaps
$$d_n^{(1)} := \frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{2}, \qquad n\ge 1.$$
For each integer $k\ge 2$, define recursively the $k$th-order derived sequence by
$$d_n^{(k)} := \frac{d_{n+1}^{(k-1)} - d_n^{(k-1)}}{2} \quad \text{(or, more generally, by iterating finite differences of the previous derived sequence).}$$
For every $k\ge 1$, answer the following three questions about the sequence $(d_n^{(k)})_{n\ge 1}$:
(a) Does $(d_n^{(k)})$ contain infinitely many prime numbers?
(b) Does $(d_n^{(k)})$ take values of the form $m!$ for infinitely many (or for any) positive integers $m$?
(c) Does $(d_n^{(k)})$ take values of the form $m^m$ for infinitely many (or for any) positive integers $m$?
artifact.status_search_result: Questions about the distribution of values in the sequence of (half-)gaps between consecutive primes and its iterated difference sequences are widely regarded as open. Even very specific subcases (e.g., whether every even number appears as a prime gap, per Polignac's conjecture, of which the twin-prime conjecture is a special case) remain unresolved, and there is no known proof that the half-gap sequence contains infinitely many primes, factorials, or numbers of the form $m^m$.

status_evidence.title: Prime gap - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Polignac's conjecture states that every positive even number k occurs as a prime gap infinitely often. The conjecture has not yet been proven or disproven for any specific value of k.
status_evidence.claim: Basic distributional questions about prime gaps remain open, including whether every even number occurs as a gap infinitely often.

status_evidence.title: The Gaps Between Primes (T5K)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known results and open problems on gaps between consecutive primes.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys list distributional questions about prime gaps as open.
